newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NAB jumps 2.3 pct on buy-back plan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NAB jumps 2.3 pct on buy-back plan.

text.p: Shares in National Australia Bank Ltd jumped 36 cents or 2.3 percent to A$16.01 in early Monday afternoon trade after announcing a plan to buy back 5.97 percent or 89.25 million of its ordinary shares.
NAB was up 50 cents or 3.2 percent on day, having risen 14 cents in earlier trade to A$15.65.
However, the share price dipped back to A$15.90 after the Australian Stock Exchange announced the correct figure of 89.25 million shares, having earlier announced a 98 million share buyback.
Analysts and brokers said the market had rallied on the immediate prospect of the buy-back, given the prospect of the buybacks had already been announced in November last year.

NAB said on November 21 in its 1996/97 annual results it planned to buy back 13 million shares, equal to the number of shares to be issued in 1997 under the dividend reinvestment, bonus share and share topup plans.
It then said on November 29 it planned to buy-back an extra 74 million shares and at the same time raise up to US$750 million through an issue of exchange tier two capital.
NAB has conducted the issue of so-called Exchangeable Capital Units (ExCaps) successfully early this month and ended up raising US$1 billion because of strong demand.
NAB said that it had announced the details of the buy-back now that the ExCap issue was complete.
It said the 89.25 million buy-back comprised the 74 million announced on November 29 plus 15.25 million shares to offset the dividend reinvestment plan, share top-up and bonus share issues.

"The group's strong capital position, combined with the flexibility provided by the ExCap issue and the continued generation of substantial capital reserves enables the group to deliver further value to shareholders through the implementation of this buy-back program," NAB managing director Don Argus said in a statement.
He said the group would continue to pursue the development of capital management initiatives.
The buy-back is scheduled to begin on April 8 and end on October 7, or whenever all the 89.25 million shares have been bought back, whichever is first.- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
